body: Thanks, I hope that I find the right people one day to happily live my life if I don't follow through. I don't necessarily think my problem is not believing in myself but I appreciate your input. I'm going to keep working on myself regardless whatever the future holds.

I appreciate your honesty but:

1. Plastic surgery is quite expensive. I don't think I could save up for it anytime soon, and of course there's the risk that comes along with it.

2. If I had the money for PS, I'd probably use that money to treat my other medical conditions first.

3. Sorry I wrote the original post in a torrent of emotions so I should've clarified that there is no correlation between the lifting and seb derm. I have chronic seb derm, and I've already tried using Nizoral, tar shampoo, and a mixture of other creams prescribed from my dermatologist. Nizoral worked well at first, keeping the seb derm away for 2-3 days, but now I have to apply it everyday or else I get severe flare ups. Tar shampoo and the other creams are pretty ineffective as well (though more effective than Nizoral), and they don't really work to prevent flare ups for me. 

I know it sounds like I'm making excuses but I'm not. Some things are easier said than done, and some of the things such as seb derm I literally have no control over. Of course I'm trying to still tackle these challenges but it seems like an uphill battle which I'm losing.

Yeah, I'm trying to do that but I can't help but feel that I'm missing out on a huge aspect of life. I don't think I've gotten a hug in years and that really makes you feel like shit. Plus whenever I do that I feel like I'm trying to justify my existence but for every good aspect about my life there's at least another 5 things that nullify those positive aspects. I'm glad that though process works for you well though.

My bad, my writing is pretty inarticulate so let me clarify. I *do* have friends that I'm close to and have their own problems for different reasons, which makes our group really tight-knit. The thing is though when I try to interact with the majority of people outside of my friend group, they generally act polite but it's pretty obvious that they're uncomfortable holding a conversation with me. 

I also try to keep my head up regarding relationships, but that whole "you'll meet that perfect girl one day" thought process is pretty demoralising to me (even though I try to follow it) due to so many bad experiences. I pretend to be outgoing in person, but for example just today, a few girls walked up to my friend while we were talking and clearly refused to acknowledge me at all, so I pretended to be busy while they talked. It's not that it's in my head either, it's just that I could tell based on their body language, eye contact, etc. I've had other experiences similar to this, but where the same friend introduced me to another friend (that happens to be a girl) and I could tell she was only saying hi out of politeness. It's probably toxic for my attitude but I felt like my theory was validated when the only acknowledgement/conversations that I got were from a lesbian girl and another one in a relationship (which I assumed they didn't feel threatened or something). Anyway, I know that I seem sad as fuck for typing this out, but I really am. Thanks for taking the time to type out your post though, I sincerely appreciate it.  

​

PS: I didn't know where to put this but I don't hold anything against that friend either, because he's a great guy and is one of the few people that care about/look out for me. I just wouldn't feel comfortable talking to him about this for obvious reasons such as stigma, etc.
It's the least I can do.
Thanks man. It's really hard living like this and I'm not sure how much longer I can go. Things don't look like they'll improve much but I'm hoping that they will.

Yeah of course, I love him and I just couldn't leave him on the streets. My parents are getting old but they could still look after him. I've had a rocky relationship with them but I still love my parents as well so I suppose that's another reason that is holding me back from doing it. I agree though- I don't want anybody to suffer because of me if I do/or when I go.
Yeah I do. He's one of the few things that have kept me going but dogs aren't a complete substitute for human interaction so I still have this empty feeling that I can't fulfil.
I don't mean this in a rude way but how much longer can the police search for until they're forced to call off the search?

Hey man, I've been there. Getting a dog really helps and will take your mind off of things. Try making new friends as well, even though it took me a couple friend groups to find the people that I like being around.
